parties: M. K. Sons Fine Jewels Limited; Book Running Lead Manager: Aryaman Financial Services Limited
headline: Kanga & Co assists M. K. Sons Fine Jewels on IPO
sum: M. K. Sons Fine Jewels, a retail jewellery chain, has proposed an IPO of up to 1.70 crore equity shares (13.6 cr fresh issue, 3.4 cr offer for sale), with Kanga & Co advising the issuer and BRLM Aryaman Financial Services.
implication: Multi-counsel coordination on a mid-cap jewellery IPO illustrates how Tier-1 counsel often co-advise both issuer and lead manager; review SEBI ICDR and stock exchange listing rules for prospectus filing gates and escrow mechanics in the fresh-OFS split structure.
detail: M. K. Sons Fine Jewels, operating retail jewellery showrooms since 2012 across gold, diamond and CZ categories, is launching an IPO comprising 13.6 crore fresh equity shares and 3.4 crore shares offered for sale by existing holders. Kanga & Co is providing counsel to both the company and BRLM Aryaman Financial Services. The lead transaction team is headed by Senior Partner Chetan Thakkar with support from Principal Associate Tejal Patankar, Senior Associate Pooja Lalwani and four Associates.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 (SEBI ICDR)
framework.note: Central: governs IPO prospectus preparation, disclosure norms, underwriting, and fresh-issue vs. OFS mechanics.
Central: enables fresh share issuance, requires shareholder approval via special resolution for IPO.

framework.ref: BSE Limited Listing Rules / NSE Limited Listing Rules
framework.note: Central: prescribe listing requirements post-IPO, continuous disclosure, and trading rules.
Governs offer document registration, stock exchange approvals, and public issue conduct.
KYC and AML compliance for issuer, promoters and significant shareholders.
Generally not triggered in IPO issuance unless combined with strategic shareholder changes.
If NRIs or foreign entities hold pre-IPO equity, review valuation and pricing constraints.
Sector-specific: M. K. Sons must comply with mandatory hallmarking for gold and precious metal jewellery.

structure.consideration: Up to ₹17 crore notional equity (1.7 crore shares × ₹10 FV); exact offer size, pricing band and subscription not yet disclosed
conditions: Shareholder approval for fresh issue and OFS
Regulatory clearances (if any sector-specific jewellery licensing required)
approvals: RTA appointment for share allotment and refund
structure.novel: Dual-counsel (Kanga advising both issuer and BRLM) on a branded retail jewellery IPO; jewellery sector IPOs remain selective in India given working capital intensity and hallmarking compliance.

triggers.note: Prospectus format, disclosure of financials, promoter background, risk factors, and use of IPO proceeds.
Fresh share issuance requires board & shareholder special resolution.

triggers.law: Hallmarking and Jewellery Quality Assurance Act, 2023
triggers.note: Issuer must maintain BIS/Government of India approved hallmarking centre accreditation and disclose compliance in prospectus.
Post-listing governance, board composition, audit committee, related-party transaction disclosure.
